rows.notes: The study is a narrative review (labelled 'Review' in the journal header; Section 1 states it 'reviews the basis of the most common methods based on RS for ET assessment'). It reports no own experiment, survey or model run. The statements that satellite-based systems reflect actual canopy conditions, cover large areas and increase field-work efficiency (Section 3.3) are authors' assertions, and the only water-saving figures (about 18% savings and 25-30% peak savings in the IRRISAT Campania case, Section 3.2) are cited from a third-party web source [144], not the authors' own result. Figures 2 and 4 are illustrative displays of NDVI/Kcb curves and AEMET ETo forecasts, not an evaluation of the claimed effect. Hence Q1 is 'no' and all other questions are 'no' by rule.

notes: Full text appears complete (pages 1-25 with references). Some pages are duplicated/garbled from PDF extraction, but content is readable. The paper is a review and provides no primary data for any claim.
